CONCEPT: a citizen of the Oxygen Nation, of the Water House. A female personification character with a mountain spring welling up between mossy stones into a clear pool, with a carved stone spout as her motif — the object reimagined as a woman in cloth and ornament that carry its materials, colors, shape and motifs. She does NOT hold, carry or wield the object; it is not a separate object. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.
ELEMENT TRAITS of Oxygen (O) to carry in her design and the scene: breath and fire and rust in one: cool clear air as translucent cloth, bright combustion orange as accents, the quiet power to corrode, the deep blue of oceans and the green of forests; it is the element of life and burning. Palette: sea blue, forest green, clear white, combustion orange.
HOUSE TRAITS of Water: water as it lives on the ground: sea, river, well and drinking water — deep blues and greens, flowing fabric, reflected light; the holding, life-giving side of water. Palette: deep sea blue, river green, white foam, sand.
AGE: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
SILHOUETTE: slender and full-busted, narrow-waisted build; long straight hair with curtain bangs; clear glass-blue hair with bright highlights.
FACE — she must read as her own person at a glance, NOT the style's default pretty face and not a sister of the other characters: first impression — a clear, innocent purity; fair skin; oval face; large eyes — large round eyes, level outer eye corners; soft rounded brows; small button nose; small bow lips; leaf-green eyes; rosy flushed cheeks.
WORLD — FANTASY: a sanctuary of forest and sea: breathing ancient trees, a coral temple at the shore, an eternal sacred flame that never consumes its altar, clean bright air. COSTUME (citizen, fantasy): her object leads — its silhouette, parts and materials must read at first glance in her outfit and headpiece, the object reimagined as cloth, forged pieces and ornament; the fantasy era only sets the period cut and finish — cloth, leather, forged metal, subtle magical glow. No corset, no modern material, no machinery. LIGHT: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise.
STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp costume and prop detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and campaign-quality lighting.
EXPOSURE (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — a deep open neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or a short hem where the outfit allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Chest and pelvis covered; no corset; keep the object's shape, material and palette.
OUTPUT: one character image that works as card art. Vertical 2:3 frame, full body with head and feet inside the frame with clear margins, face turned toward the camera (front or three-quarter). Standing, card-ready pose; the environment may be rich while her design stays fully readable.
EXPRESSION: one brow raised higher, head tilted, eyes wide and attentive, lips slightly parted.
BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose or the frame.
ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no living creature, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (O) and atomic number (8) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.
ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, both hands drawn correctly as hands. No extra limbs.
